name: Robotic Grasping and Manipulation Competition (RGMC) Manufacturing Track
ability_definition: The ability to make precisely coordinated movements of the fingers of one or both hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble very small objects.

task_realism.reasoning: The NIST assembly task boards use real industrial small parts: pegs, gears, nuts and bolts, belts, wires, and connectors. These are inserted and removed at realistic tolerances, closely mirroring small-parts assembly and disassembly work. Some realism is lost because the board is a standardized fixture, not a real product. It also omits flexible, deformable, or very tiny items like springs, washers, and fine wires in cluttered bins.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: It runs on real physical hardware with randomized board and kit layouts and a time limit. This captures real-world noise, contact dynamics, and positioning variance better than simulation. However, the competition environment is controlled. CAD data is available in advance and the part set is known. There is no sustained throughput over shifts, no defect variability, and no interruptions. These conditions are more favorable than a real production line.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It measures the outcome of small-part grasping, orienting, and insertion. The ability, however, is about precisely coordinated movement of the fingers. Because the track is end-effector-agnostic, parallel grippers and hand tools can solve tasks without any multi-finger coordination or in-hand manipulation. It also omits bimanual finger coordination, tactile fine adjustment on very small objects, and handling of delicate or deformable parts.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are real physical components and kits, and outputs are physically assembled or disassembled boards scored per part. This closely resembles real assembly work products and pass/fail inspection. The main artificial elements are the point-based scoring and the time bonus, which are competition constructs rather than workplace quality metrics, and the standardized board layout.

transferability_reasoning: RGMC's Manufacturing Track is one of the more realistic tests of small-parts assembly, using real hardware, real industrial components, and randomized layouts. That gives it solid task realism and format match. Its transfer to Finger Dexterity specifically is limited because it scores task outcomes regardless of end-effector, so gripper- or tool-based solutions can succeed without demonstrating coordinated finger movement. Its controlled, CAD-informed competition setting is also easier than real production conditions.

2020.model_or_system: Team SDU Robotics (University of Southern Denmark) robot system
2020.metric: competition points (task maximum 273 = 92 disassembly + 181 assembly, plus a time bonus for finishing early)
2020.human_reference: Specialist workforce: electromechanical and small-parts assemblers who do fine manual assembly (pegs, gears, belts, nuts and bolts, wire routing) in manufacturing settings.
